questions.q: What does the January bank statement show for payment PMT-21087 that doesn't match the GL?
options: The bank shows no debit for PMT-21087 at all
The bank shows two $9,200.00 debits, while the GL shows exactly one
The bank shows the payment for the wrong amount, $18,400.00
The bank shows the payment going to the wrong supplier
questions.explain: The bank statement shows PMT-21087 debited twice, $9,200.00 each, while LTV's own GL and Cash Management records show exactly one $9,200.00 disbursement, matching what actually happened on LTV's side.

questions.q: Which transactions reconcile automatically without issue in this lesson?
options: Harborview's $55,100.00 deposit and PMT-21094's $18,400.00 EFT, among other routine items
No transactions reconcile automatically this period
Only transactions under the Canadian ledger
questions.explain: Harborview's deposit, the $18,400.00 Meridian EFT, and routine smaller items all match one bank line to one GL line without issue.

questions.q: What is the size of the unreconciled variance this lesson flags?
questions.explain: The duplicate bank debit creates a $9,200.00 unreconciled variance, flagged but not yet explained.

questions.q: Why does this lesson stop short of resolving the $9,200.00 variance?
options: Because Oracle Fusion automatically resolves bank variances overnight
Because resolving it requires contacting the bank to confirm and reverse a duplicate transmission — a cross-system investigation reserved for Chapter 3
Because the variance is immaterial and does not need resolution
Because Grace Olsen is on leave for the rest of January
questions.explain: Confirming the duplicate transmission with Regions Bank and getting it reversed is exactly the kind of investigation Chapter 3 is built around, so it's carried forward as an open item here.

questions.q: Why is this problem described as different from the AP accrual or AR misapplication problems?
options: It involves a larger dollar amount than the others
It is visible immediately upon running a routine bank reconciliation, rather than hidden in a journal or invoice-level detail
It is the only problem that affects the Canadian ledger
It is the only problem caused by a system error rather than a process error
questions.explain: Unlike the GRNI accrual or the AR misapplication, which are invisible until specifically investigated, this variance shows up the moment a bank reconciliation is run — which is why Elena Marsh already knows about it.
